column1: # REGISTER 4 (PARTIAL) - mutation-proofs.wave6-ulichney.tsv
# Wave-6 proofs for ONE guard: reference-impl/tests/test_scatter.py, specifically the nine rows
# added with the Ulichney (1993) void-and-cluster tiles that close OPEN-ITEMS #22. Written here
# and NOT into the shared mutation-proofs.tsv, which other agents are filling at the same time.
# Merge target: the test_scatter.py row of mutation-proofs.tsv.
# EVERY CELL BELOW IS FROM EXECUTION, none predicted. Harness for each trial:
#   1. read reference-impl/scatter.py into memory     4. restore the file from memory
#   2. apply the edit - SUBJECT ONLY; no mutation     5. after the last trial, `git diff --stat --
#      is ever applied to a test file                    scatter.py` read 181 insertions and 0
#   3. `python -m pytest tests/test_scatter.py -q`        deletions - HEAD plus the new block and
#      from reference-impl/, then narrowed to the         nothing else, so every trial's restore
#      target row alone for its first E line              was byte-exact. (Prose in the module
#                                                         docstring and two comment lines were
#                                                         reflowed AFTER the trials, which is why
#                                                         the shipped diff reads 192 / 3.)
# Baseline for every row: `16 passed in 2.38s`, 0 failed.
# DENOMINATOR
#   new guard rows added to test_scatter.py .................. 9
#   rows with a mutation that went GREEN -> RED .............. 8  (88.9%)
#   rows with a decoy that stayed GREEN ...................... 8  (88.9%)
#   rows declared DECORATIVE ................................. 1  (test_a_regular_lattice_...)
#   IDENTITY: 8 PROVEN + 1 DECORATIVE = 9 rows == 9 new tests -> HOLDS
#   A row without a decoy would prove only that the guard is noisy; a row without a mutation would
#   prove only that it is quiet. Both halves are required of a PROVEN row, so both are counted.
# THE ONE DECORATIVE ROW, stated rather than hidden. `test_a_regular_lattice_fails_the_spectrum_
# oracle_too` exists to show that the low/high power ratio alone is NOT a sufficient blue-noise
# oracle, because a regular lattice passes it (measured: lattice 0.0381, mask 0.0453, white noise
# 0.83-1.11). Three of its four clauses are facts about the test's own lattice and cannot be moved
# by any edit to scatter.py. The fourth, `mask_peak < 25.0`, does constrain the subject, and three
# single-edit mutations failed to move it (see the row). It is kept because deleting it would take
# the calibration evidence with it, and it is labelled DECORATIVE so nobody counts it as a guard.
# WHY THE WRAPAROUND HAD TO BE RESTRUCTURED BEFORE IT COULD BE PROVED. The first implementation
# put the toroidal Gaussian in a PRECOMPUTED kernel image and re-centred it with `np.roll`. That
# arrangement is circular no matter what the image holds: both candidate mutations - dropping the
# wrap replicas from the kernel sum, and replacing modular indexing with abs() - produced a
# BIT-IDENTICAL mask, because a periodic kernel indexed modularly is a circular convolution by
# construction. The tileability guard would have been unfalsifiable. `_kernel_at` now evaluates a
# minimum-image Gaussian directly, which puts the wrap in two deletable lines; row 5 is that
# deletion. A guard that could not have failed is not a guard, and the repair was to the SUBJECT'S
# STRUCTURE, not to the guard.
